accuracy.evidence: Strategy claims follow Dunlosky et al. (2013): elaborative interrogation and self-explanation rated moderate utility, rereading and highlighting low; concept maps follow Novak and Cañas (labelled linking phrases forming propositions, general-to-specific hierarchy, cross-links as evidence of integrated understanding); learner-built maps outperforming studying given maps follows Nesbit and Adesope (2006). The science content was checked against GCSE Biology (AQA 8461): arteries have thick muscular, elastic walls because blood leaves the heart at high pressure, and the elastic tissue stretches and recoils; photosynthesis needs light absorbed by chlorophyll and makes glucose and oxygen; respiration uses glucose and oxygen and releases energy. Each rejected cross-link is genuinely false. The maths steps for 3(x + 2) = 18 are correct and the 'subtract 3' feedback states the true result. Numeric items were checked at range corners.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented study-strategy errors: rereading as effective (step 1 prediction, step 5, challenge 'reread', m5), the illusion of fluency (step 5 prediction, challenge 'record'), circular why-answers that repeat the fact (step 1 feedback, m7), unlabelled or decorative map links (challenge 'nolabel' and 'pretty', m2), maps judged by size (step 3 prediction), false cross-links (step 3, challenge 'false', p3), copying maps (challenge 'copymap', m6), and describing a step instead of explaining it (step 4 'The 3 goes away', 'move it over and it changes sign', challenge 'trick' and 'copy', p5).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagcmap's mechanisms are a why-chain that grows one reason at a time, a concept map whose links must be labelled by dragging linking phrases so each reads as a true proposition, testing dashed cross-links between two branches, and self-explaining the rule behind each step of a worked equation. flaglink (ages 7-8) builds a loose web of 'is like' links, flagteach explains to a toy, flagwhy bundles tens and tests rules, flagcornell structures notes; none labels propositions or tests cross-links. lab_distinct gate passes under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner experiences the rule before it is stated: a wrong linking phrase is read back as a false sentence ('Chlorophyll needs light'), so the proposition idea comes from the map itself; the why-chain visibly lengthens only with real causes; false cross-links turn red with the reason; and the shallow habits are rejected with why they fade. The text then confirms each idea in one sentence.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: 'reading it three more times' helps memory (the chain shows what why-questions add, and the habit sort marks rereading shallow), a good map has 'lots of boxes and colours' (only true propositions count as links), and 'familiar means learned' (the sort and feedback name the illusion of fluency).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with eleven distinct wrong-answer messages: reread, highlight, nolabel, pretty, false, empty, trick, copy, record, copymap and list, each naming the specific slip.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs read at about FK grade 3 to 8 (overall under the kid limit) with a worked example in each (artery why-chain, photosynthesis link, dividing by 3); the adult text stays under the adult limit and uses the terms elaboration, elaborative interrogation, self-explanation, node, linking phrase, proposition, cross-link and illusion of fluency. Canvas labels are single words or short sentences.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Each kid paragraph teaches one strategy or the reason to prefer it; items each test a different point: elaborative answer (p1), links in a chain (p2), true proposition (p3), counting cross-links (p4), self-explanation (p5), definition (m1), linking phrases (m2), cross-link (m3), why-chain workload (m4), fluency illusion (m5), map from memory (m6), circular reasons (m7) and explaining a check (m8).

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android light and dark and iPhone 13 dark screenshots of every step at start, mid-demo and after Show me: the phrase chips wrap to two rows above the map without touching the Photosynthesis box after moving the node rows down; seven nodes, four link labels and four cross-link pills fit without overlap; the why-chain of four boxes and three answer cards fits; worked-example steps and explanations wrap; the habit card sits above two boxes. Dragging a phrase onto the link and a habit into a box was tested on iPhone 13 emulation.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: 'Because: …', 'Label: Photosynthesis makes Glucose' for each phrase, 'Test link: …' for each cross-link, 'Explain: …' and both sort boxes. The canvas aria-label is rewritten with every feedback message. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors; the dashed and active links use a lighter blue in dark theme.
